data.long_meaning: The name Vaishali is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Vaishali', which means 'City of Shining'. It is believed to be the name of a prosperous and beautiful city mentioned in ancient Indian texts. The name Vaishali carries the meaning “City of Shining” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vaishali usually hope their child will grow to embody city of shining and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Vaishali is a historically significant name in Indian culture, as it was the name of an ancient city and republic that flourished from the 6th century BCE to the 3rd century BCE. This city was located in the ancient Magadha region of eastern India and was renowned for its prosperity, economic strength, and democratic institutions. Vaishali was a leading cultural, educational, and political center of its time and played an important role in the development of Indian art, literature, and philosophy.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name Vaishali holds a spiritual significance as it is associated with Vaishnavism, a devotional tradition within Hinduism that focuses on the worship of Vishnu and his avatars, particularly Krishna and Rama. The spiritual significance of the name Vaishali stems from the belief that it represents the inner radiance and purity of the soul. The name is a reminder that just like a prosperous and beautiful city, the soul is capable of shining bright with love, wisdom, and virtue. It is also believed that the name carries the blessings of Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge, wisdom, and learning, and Laxmi, the goddess of wealth, prosperity, and happiness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vaishali: Radiant and virtuous, embodying the purity and wisdom of the sacred sacred text, the Vedas. The name evokes the strength and grace of the legendary city of Vaishali, where Lady Mahavira, the twenty-fourth Tirthankara, graced the earth with her presence.

vedic_reference.root_origin: Vaiśālī, a city mentioned in Mahabharata
vedic_reference.note: Vaishali was an ancient Indian city located in the present-day Bihar state of India, mentioned in Mahabharata. It is famous for its association with Buddhism, Jainism, and its ancient ruins. The city is believed to be the birthplace of Emperor Ashoka, and it is also mentioned in the epic as a place where Bhishma Pitamaha spent his last days on the bed of arrows.

historical_references.reference: Vaishali was an ancient Indian republic and major trading center located in the Magadha region. It is believed to have been founded by the Videha King, Chedi, around 600 BCE.
historical_references.context: Ancient Indian republic and major trading center

historical_references.reference: Vaishali was also a significant center of Buddhism. The Buddha is said to have visited the city thrice and is believed to have preached his last sermon there, at the Mulgandhakuti Vihara, before his death in 528 BCE.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Vaishali continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
